findings.title: PEFT/LoRA resume silently restores no adapter weights: the model continues from fresh random init while the accountant, noise counter, sampler cursor and optimizer state are all restored
findings.claim: `_load_model_weights` restores a PEFT checkpoint with `self._model.load_state_dict(new_state, strict=not self._is_peft)`. PEFT's `save_pretrained` writes `adapter_model.safetensors` with the adapter name stripped from every key (`...lora_A.weight`), while the live module's `state_dict()` keys carry it (`...lora_A.default.weight`). With `strict=False` every saved key is 'unexpected' and every model key is 'missing', so the call is a complete no-op; the returned `_IncompatibleKeys` is discarded and nothing is logged. The resumed run therefore trains from the *freshly initialised* adapter while `dp_state.pt` (clip/noise/sampler state), `dp_optimizer.pt` and `accountant.json` are all restored faithfully. HuggingFace's own Trainer, whose parity DPTrainer claims, uses `model.load_adapter(resume_from_checkpoint, active_adapter, is_trainable=True)` for exactly this case (.venv transformers/trainer.py:3440, and :3502 for load_best_model_at_end).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced end to end on the real trainer: tiny GPT-2 + LoRA(r=4, target_modules=['c_attn']), 4 steps, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2. Instrumenting `_load_model_weights` printed `_is_peft: True`, `loaded-file keys: ['base_model.model.transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.lora_A.weight', ...]`, `weights changed by load?: False`, `post-load == fresh-init?: True`, `post-load == checkpoint?: False`. Consequence in a full run (dropout disabled so the trajectory is otherwise deterministic): continuous run logs grad_norm 0.836132824 at step 3 and 0.929508567 at step 4; the resumed run logs 1.277820706 and 1.491086841 for the same steps with the same batches (batch_size 3 then 1 in both) and the same reported epsilon (0.286266566, 0.413383073); final |Δw| over the LoRA tensors = 0.1716. A user resuming a long DP fine-tune therefore silently throws away all learned adapter weights, keeps spending privacy budget, and gets a completed run with a plausible epsilon and a garbage model. `load_best_model_at_end=True` hits the identical code at :4910-4912, so the 'best' adapter is never loaded either.

findings.title: DP-SGD resume keeps the checkpoint's Poisson sample_rate in the sampler but rebuilds the accountant from the new args, so a batch-size change on resume under-reports epsilon behind a log.warning
findings.claim: `_from_state_dict_poisson` deliberately takes `sample_rate` and `truncated_batch_size` from the snapshot and ignores the template, while `_build_mechanism` builds the accountant's `poisson(gaussian(nm), sample_rate=...)` from the *current* `TrainingArguments` (`ctx.sample_rate = train_batch_size / dataset_size`). `sample_rate` is tagged `drift="dp_relevant"` in `RuntimeCheckpoint`, but for `mechanism_kind == "gaussian"` (every DP-SGD run) `_warn_on_arg_drift` only logs a warning and continues. The result is that the sampler runs at the saved q while the accountant charges the new q. This is the exact defect OPQ-322 / closed issue #792 described for `RandomAllocationSampler.num_bins`; the fix (#1019, `fix(dpsgd)!: reject allocation-law drift on sampler restore`) added a `k`/`t`/`allocation` equality guard to `KOutOfTSampler` only. The sibling samplers still resolve the same class of parameter in favour of the snapshot: `PoissonSampler` (`sample_rate`, `truncated_batch_size`), `CyclicPoissonSampler` (`sample_rate`, `bands`, `partition_type`), `BMinSepSampler` (`bands`, `sampling_prob`), `BallsInBinsSampler` (`num_bins`), `SequentialBatchSampler` (`batch_size`). `truncated_batch_size` is not a `RuntimeCheckpoint` field at all, so drifting it produces no warning whatsoever.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced on the real trainer (dataset N=64, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5, 8 steps, save_steps=4). Phase 1 at per_device_train_batch_size=32 (q=0.5) realises batch sizes [32,25,29,31,36,26,41,36] and ends at epsilon=4.75151. Resuming checkpoint-4 with per_device_train_batch_size=8 (q=0.125) realises [36,26,41,36] for steps 5-8 — bit-identical to the q=0.5 continuous run, i.e. the sampler is still drawing at q=0.5 — and reports epsilon=3.25344. The resumed `accountant.json` contains four `"sample_rate": 0.125` Poisson nodes for the post-resume steps while `dp_state.pt`'s `sampler_state` records `sample_rate: 0.5`. Reported epsilon is 31.5 % below the epsilon of the mechanism that actually ran (true 4.75151 vs reported 3.25344). The only diagnostics are three `log.warning` lines ('Resume arg drift on sample_rate (dp_relevant, DP-SGD): saved=0.5, current=0.125', plus expected_steps_per_epoch and expected_batch_size), none of which says which value won.

findings.title: Full-finetune resume and load_best_model_at_end crash for every tied-embedding model because the checkpoint omits lm_head.weight but the loader is strict
findings.claim: `_save_model_artifacts` writes checkpoint weights with `self._model.save_pretrained(output_dir, safe_serialization=...)`, which drops tied parameters (`_tied_weights_keys`) from the file. `_load_model_weights` then reads that file and calls `load_state_dict(new_state, strict=True)` for every non-PEFT model, so the missing `lm_head.weight` is a hard error. findings.title: MF noise state carries no derivation-version or execution-identity tag except for BISR, so the #1018 lambda-CGD stream change and any strategy-hyperparameter drift restore silently onto a different mechanism
findings.claim: `MFNoiseState`'s wire format records only `layout_version`, `_step_counter`, `_rng_key`, the max-norm latch and the inner-state field *names*. It records neither the strategy hyperparameters (bands, max_buffers, momentum, alpha/beta, lambda_, normalized), the horizon (`n_steps`, `min_sep`, `max_participations`), the compute dtype, nor a version of the noise-derivation law. `d09d7b9a fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth (#886)` gave BISR exactly such an execution identity (`_BisrExecutionIdentity(version, inverse_coefficients, normalized, n_steps, compute_dtype)`, `_bisr.py:42-51, 92-119`) and BISR consequently fails closed on all of these. No sibling strategy got one. `f2d90d61 fix(random)!: namespace lambda-CGD noise stream (#1018)` then changed lambda-CGD's per-step key derivation from `fold_in(key, step)` to `_mf_gaussian_column_key(key, step)` without bumping `_LAYOUT_VERSION` (still 1) or `DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION` (still 7 at that commit). The trainer path is currently protected only by coincidence: an unrelated commit two hours later, `873de427 delete(dpsgd)!: remove unsupported bounded Gaussian noise (#1021)`, bumped the bundle to 8, and all four released tags in the delta (v0.15.4, v0.15.5.rc1, v0.15.5.rc2, v0.15.6.rc1) write 7. The library-level resume path — `opaque.serialization.state_dict(noise_state)` -> torch.save -> `from_state_dict` — has no guard at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed: a lambda-CGD `MFNoiseState` produced with the pre-#1018 derivation (monkeypatched back to `fold_in(key, step)`) and serialised at step 4 is accepted verbatim by HEAD's `from_state_dict` with no error; the step-4 release then differs from what the uninterrupted pre-#1018 run would emit ([0.33594, 1.21912, 0.66765] vs [1.37039, 0.54192, -0.19998]). Because C^-1 for lambda-CGD is 2-banded, the correlation term at the resume step multiplies a z_{s-1} drawn from the new stream that was never released at step s-1, so the realised operator is not the lambda-CGD strategy matrix the accountant priced. The same silence covers config drift on every non-BISR strategy: restoring a band_mf state into a template built with `n_steps` 8->16 is ACCEPTED and emits different noise (-0.76381 -> -0.70943); `momentum` 1.0->0.5 ACCEPTED (-0.76381 -> -1.01377); bsr `alpha` 0.9->0.7 ACCEPTED (-1.10275 -> -1.03146); lambda_cgd `lambda_` 0.5->0.9 ACCEPTED (-1.27672 -> -1.77366). BISR rejects the corresponding drifts with 'BISR checkpoint execution identity does not match the configured runtime'. `GaussianNoiseState` has the same shape of hole for `compute_dtype`, whose wire format is `{_step_counter, _rng_key.seed, _rng_key.impl}` only.

findings.title: DDP resume installs rank 0's sampler snapshot on every rank, silently re-correlating the per-rank Poisson masks that the per-rank key fold exists to keep independent
findings.line: 3879-3885 (the acknowledging comment, 'written once on rank 0' at :3881), 3944-3949 (per-rank fold), 5036 + 5197 (rank-0-only `_save_dp_runtime`), 1861-1877 (unconditional restore on every rank, `from_state_dict` at :1875)
findings.claim: For `world_size > 1` the trainer folds the rank into the sampler key so each shard draws an independent Bernoulli(q) mask. The sampler snapshot inside `dp_state.pt` stores the concrete stream key (`key_seed`/`key_impl`) and is written only on the saving rank (`if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` at :5036), while `_inner_training_loop` restores it on every rank (`ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` at :1875-1877, with no rank branch). After a resume every rank therefore samples the same local positions. The in-code comment at :3879-3885 acknowledges this and justifies deferring it with 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected'. That justification is not sufficient: Poisson amplification requires a record's inclusion indicator to be independent of the rest of the sample, not merely Bernoulli(q) marginally. Under a shared mask the records sharing a local index across the `world_size` shards are included or excluded together, so conditioning on the rest of the batch can reveal the target record's inclusion bit, which is precisely what the amplification hides. No warning is emitted at resume time, and no test covers it (the `distributed` marker lane has no sampler-snapshot case).
findings.failure_scenario: world_size=4, per-rank shard length L, q=0.25. Phase 1: rank r uses key fold_in(seed, r), so the four shards' masks are independent and the global sample is an i.i.d. Poisson sample — the model the `poisson(gaussian(nm), q)` accountant prices. Resume from any checkpoint: all four ranks restore rank 0's `key_seed`, so the record at local index i is now included on all four shards simultaneously. For a neighbouring pair differing in one record x at local index i0, the three co-indexed records on the other shards are included exactly when x is; when their clipped gradients are large relative to sigma = nm*C the aggregate reveals the shared inclusion bit, and conditioned on it the released pair is the *unamplified* Gaussian rather than the q-subsampled one. The accountant continues to charge the amplified per-step PLD for every post-resume step, so the reported epsilon is an underestimate whose size grows with world_size and with 1/nm. I did not run a two-rank Gloo reproduction (the behaviour is asserted by the code comment itself and follows directly from the rank-0-only save plus the unconditional restore), so the magnitude is reasoned, not measured.

findings.title: Optimizer-state restore silently degrades to template defaults when the optimizer or parameter set changes across a resume
findings.line: 65-73 (`_tensor_load` returns the template when the key is absent); /home/user/opaque/packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/_structural.py:110-112; /home/user/opaque/packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5567
findings.claim: The generic loader is template-driven and intentionally tolerant: `_tensor_load` returns the template tensor when its slot is missing from the state dict, and `walk_load` on a Mapping iterates only the template's keys so extra saved keys are dropped. `_apply_runtime_state` feeds `dp_optimizer.pt` straight into `from_state_dict(ctx.opt_state, opt_sd)` and `optim` is not among `RuntimeCheckpoint`'s `compare_on_resume` fields, so changing the optimizer across a resume neither raises nor warns — the run continues with a state object whose step counter came from the old optimizer and whose moment buffers are zeros.

Restoring a 2-parameter checkpoint into a 3-parameter template is likewise accepted, with the new parameter's `mu` silently zero. MFNoiseState fails closed on structural drift: tested a 16-case save/restore matrix across band_mf/blt/bisr/bsr/identity/lambda_cgd — bands 2<->4, bandwidth 3<->5, band_mf<->blt, band_mf<->identity all raise CheckpointError with shape or inner-state-manifest messages, and the restored RNG key correctly overrides a different template key (seed 7 snapshot into a seed-99 template reproduces the seed-7 stream).

BISR bounded streaming state (#886) is the strongest codec in the tree: `_BisrStreamingState` carries a layout version plus a full `_BisrExecutionIdentity` (inverse_coefficients, normalized, n_steps, compute_dtype, version), rejects unversioned legacy dense-history checkpoints by name, validates the history length against the bandwidth and the step against the horizon. Verified by restoring across bandwidth 3->5 and n_steps 8->16 (both rejected with field-level diagnostics).

Trainer prefetch cursor clamp (#1009 / OPQ-321) verified empirically: with dataloader_num_workers 0 and 2, both `poisson` and `k_out_of_t` snapshots at checkpoint-4 record consumed=4 (== global_step), i.e. worker prefetch no longer leaks into the saved cursor. The load-side clamp at _dp_trainer.py:1276-1292 also re-clamps consumed>global_step with a warning.

k-out-of-t allocation-law guard (#1019) is present and correct: `_from_state_dict_k_out_of_t` type-and-value-checks k, t and allocation against the template and raises ConfigurationError; the saved key is the domain-separated stream key so the restored stream is the saved one.

Sampler RNG namespacing (#884) is checkpoint-compatible in both directions: `_state_dict_poisson` persists the *effective* NumPy stream seed and `_from_state_dict_poisson` bypasses the constructor's fold via `_from_stream_key`, and `_sample_step` was untouched by the commit — so a pre-#884 snapshot (raw key seed) still replays the stream it originally ran. Verified by restoring a hand-built pre-#884 state dict.

Accountant JSON round-trip: loaded a real checkpoint's accountant.json, re-serialised it and confirmed the JSON is byte-identical, epsilon reproduces (3.3327138885497596 at delta=1e-5), and the whole composition spine (CachedProcess/Repeated/Composed) survives.

Template-budget preservation (#887 / OPQ-302) works: `from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, 1e-5)), sd)` keeps the template budget when the checkpoint has none, and `budget_exceeded` correctly becomes True afterwards.

DpProcess codec fails closed on the removed accounting types: `_load_dp_process`/`_load_leaf` raise `Unknown DpProcess type` for names no longer in `_PROCESS_REGISTRY` (PerStep and RandomAllocation removed by #894/#761) and `unexpected keys for X` / `missing required field` for the renamed KOutOfT fields, so no pre-removal accountant.json can be silently reinterpreted. Adaptive-clipping state round-trips completely: all eleven fields (_current_clipping_norm, _next_clipping_norm, _step, _rng_key, _fraction_noise_std, _learning_rate, _target_quantile, _clipping_norm_min/_max, _num_clipped, _batch_size) are persisted and the snapshot wins over a drifted template, so the DP quantile release cannot silently change its noise scale on resume.

MF horizon-calibration resume guard (OPQ-319 / #789) is in place: `_validate_horizon_resume_calibration` rejects calibration-mode drift and privacy_target_epsilon drift for horizon processes, and `_setup_training` pins the saved multiplier via `resume_horizon_noise_multiplier` instead of recalibrating, so the sigma-mixing path is closed.
